summary: Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar (1909–2001) was an Indologist. He earned an M.A. at the University of Mumbai and a doctorate at Heidelberg University. He held professorships at Fergusson College and Savitribai Phule Pune University, and served at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Ramesh Chandra Negi is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He taught Ruth Gamble and Andy Rotman, and held posts as Research Assistant (attested 2001–2004) and Associate Professor (attested 2026) at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Ramesh Chandra Majumdar (1888–1980) was a historian and Indologist who studied at Ripon College, Brojomohun College, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta. He held leadership posts at the University of Dhaka, Banaras Hindu University, and the Indian History Congress.

Ramesh Shankar Gupte worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. In 1967, he was attested as Head of History & Ancient Indian Culture at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and held visiting lectureships at Wake Forest, Salem, and Winston-Salem State.
Ramin Etesami is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College (attested 2015), supervised by Lobsang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina.
Ramkrishna Bhattacharya (1947–2022) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1968–1970) and held a post at Ananda Mohan College (~1973–2007).
Ramon Prats is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts attested at Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources (1999) and Pompeu Fabra University (2017).

Ran Mao is a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied at Hainan University and Kasetsart University (PhD 2020). He taught Chinese at institutions including Hainan, KU Leuven, and Ludovika University, and held a post at Guizhou University (2020–2022).
Randall Studstill is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied under Steven D. Goodman and completed his doctoral work under the supervision of Richard K. Payne.

Randy J. LaPolla is a linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist who earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under James Alan Matisoff. He served as professor at City University of Hong Kong and Beijing Normal University.

Rangama Chandawimala is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Kakkapalliye Anuruddha. He is attested as an Associate Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (2026).

Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (1924–1981) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught numerous students, including Chögyam Trungpa, Pema Chödrön, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

Raniero Gnoli (1930–2025) was an Italian Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Mario Praz. He served as Professor of Indology at Sapienza University of Rome from 1964 to 2000.
Ranjeet Kumar Verma is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Lucknow. In 2025, he held a scholar post at the Indian Institute of Technology (ISM) Dhanbad.
Rano Hodžiakbarovna Guljamova (1940–1985) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. She studied at the National University of Uzbekistan from ~1957 to 1962 and taught there from 1962 until 1985.
Ranu Kunwar pursued PhD studies at the Australian National University (2022–2026) under the doctoral supervision of Assa Doron (attested 2026).

Raoul Birnbaum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He held a post attested at Santa Clara University (2012) and served as professor of Buddhist studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz (attested 2003, 2017).

Raoul Curiel (1913–2000) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Alfred Foucher, among others. He held key posts at the DAFA, Pakistan's Department of Archaeology, and the Cabinet des Médailles.
Raphael Kühner (1802–1878) was a linguist. He studied at Ernestinum Gotha and the University of Göttingen (~1821–1824), and he taught Georg Bühler.
Raphael Marozzi (1913–1999) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He completed a B.A. at the University of Washington (–1949) and an M.A. at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1949–1952).
